property_summary: For any caller who is the current owner and calls setOwner(target), the contract's owner public getter equals the provided target address after the call; the mutant that assigns tx.origin instead can break this by making owner == tx.origin != target when the call is proxied (msg.sender != tx.origin).

If a current owner calls setOwner(via) to set owner to a target address, then after the call the contract's owner must equal the provided target; the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin will break this when msg.sender != tx.origin (i.e., when the call is proxied through a contract), because owner becomes the external tx.origin instead of the provided target.

For any proxy contract address P (fuzzed) that the current owner uses to call setOwner(target), when the call succeeds the reference sets owner to the provided target address, but the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin will instead set owner to the original transaction origin (not the provided target) when msg.sender != tx.origin—so owner == target for all admissible inputs in the reference, and some proxied inputs will break the mutant.

For any caller that is the immediate msg.sender (including contracts) the correct contract sets owner to the provided _owner after a successful setOwner call; the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin will break this when the call is proxied through an intermediate contract (msg.sender != tx.origin) because owner becomes tx.origin instead of the provided _owner.

For any caller who is the current owner and any target address _owner, after calling setOwner(_owner) the contract's public owner getter equals the provided _owner; the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin breaks this when the owner call is proxied through another contract (msg.sender != tx.origin), causing owner to become tx.origin instead of the provided _owner.

For every caller who is the owner, calling setOwner(_owner) completes (does not revert) and returns true while updating the public owner to _owner; the mutant sometimes returns false even though it still updates owner, violating the rule that setOwner called by the owner always returns true on success.

For any caller who is the current owner and any address _owner, calling setOwner(_owner) succeeds (does not revert) and returns true — the mutant sometimes returns false despite succeeding, breaking this rule.
